question.text: Manoj is a distributor evaluating the IT infrastructure of an AIF during operational DD. Which finding would be MOST concerning?

answer.text: The fund uses cloud-based portfolio management software with encryption
The fund has implemented two-factor authentication for all system access
The fund has no disaster recovery plan and stores all data on a single local server without backup
The fund conducts annual cybersecurity audits

explanation.text: The Logic: A lack of any disaster-recovery plan combined with single-server, no-backup data storage exposes a fund to catastrophic data loss from hardware failure, natural disaster, or cyberattack. The other options describe positive IT-infrastructure controls. The Trap: Cloud-based systems, two-factor authentication, and annual cybersecurity audits are all positive controls — none alone is a concerning finding. Note: The XIX-A workbook supports general data-privacy / cyber-crime / data-theft DD considerations at the distributor level. It does not separately enumerate disaster-recovery plans, offsite backup, RTOs, or DR testing as specific AIF operational-DD checks; treat those as general operational-DD knowledge applicable to any fund.
